pred_args.text:
Can a Virus Change Our DNA? What You Need to Know

Viruses are tiny germs that can only multiply inside the cells of a living host, such as a person. You may have heard that some viruses can “change your DNA.” The truth is more subtle.

Most viruses do not rewrite your genetic code. When a virus infects a cell, it may insert its own genetic material into the cell’s DNA. This inserted viral material is called a provirus. Usually it stays quiet and does not damage or change your genes.

In rare cases, however, the viral genetic material can land in the wrong spot. If it disrupts an important gene, it may cause a genetic mutation. But this is uncommon and is not the main way viruses make people sick. More often, viruses cause illness by using your cells to copy themselves, which can damage or kill the cells and trigger inflammation.

So can a virus modify human DNA? It can insert genetic material into our DNA, and in rare instances that can cause a mistake in a gene. But everyday viral infections do not typically go around rewriting our genetic code.
